memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The Lord said to Aaron, "You, your sons and your family are to bear the responsibility for offenses connected with the sanctuary, and you and your sons alone are to bear the responsibility for offenses connected with the priesthood. Bring your fellow Levites from your ancestral tribe to join you and assist you when you and your sons minister before the tent of the covenant law." — Num 18:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
After the people's terrified cry at the end of the last chapter — "Are we all going to die?" — God answers with reassurance and order. He speaks directly to Aaron and establishes clearly who bears responsibility for the sanctuary. The people need not live in dread, because God has appointed those who will carry the weight of drawing near on their behalf.

Notice the language: the priests are "to bear the responsibility." Serving God was not merely a privilege; it carried genuine accountability. Those who ministered in holy things stood in a place of great trust, answerable for how the sacred was handled. With nearness to God came real weight.

This is a helpful reminder for all who serve God in any capacity. Leadership and service in holy things are not to be taken lightly. Whether we teach, lead, care for others, or serve in quiet ways, we handle things that matter to God, and we are accountable to Him for how we do it. Reverence and responsibility go together.

Yet there is comfort woven through the weight. The priests bore responsibility so the people could be at peace. And this points us to our great High Priest, Jesus, who bore the ultimate responsibility for our sins. He carried what we could never carry, standing in our place before a holy God. Where the priests of old bore responsibility imperfectly and had to be replaced, Christ bore it perfectly and forever. Because He carried the weight, we can draw near without fear.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you take your service to God seriously as a sacred responsibility?
2. In what area has God entrusted you with something that matters to Him?
3. How does it comfort you that Christ bore the ultimate responsibility for your sin?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, help me to serve You with reverence, taking seriously the responsibility You entrust to me. Thank You that Jesus, my great High Priest, bore the weight of my sin so that I can draw near without fear. Amen.
